items.stem: A product earns a 40% contribution margin. If price is cut by 10%, roughly how much must volume rise just to hold contribution?

options.text: More than proportionally, because the margin cushion shrinks when price falls
options.rationale: Correct: a lower margin requires a disproportionate volume gain to break even.
Volume must rise more than 10% because margin falls.

options.text: Volume can fall and contribution still holds
options.rationale: Falling volume cannot offset a price cut.

options.text: No change in volume is needed
options.rationale: Contribution would drop without a volume rise.

items.explanation: Correct: a lower margin requires a disproportionate volume gain to break even.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO are risks of habitual deep discounting? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Customers learn to delay purchases until the next discount
options.rationale: Correct: discounting can train buying behaviour.

options.text: The reference price in customers' minds is eroded
options.rationale: Correct: frequent discounts lower perceived value.

options.text: Contribution margin per unit automatically rises
options.rationale: Discounting lowers, not raises, unit margin.
Deep discounting tends to weaken a premium.

items.explanation: Correct: discounting can train buying behaviour.

items.stem: A large customer generates the most revenue but demands heavy service and discounts. The best profitability view is to:

options.text: Measure contribution after cost to serve, not revenue alone
options.rationale: Correct: cost to serve can turn a big account unprofitable.

options.text: Rank them top because revenue is highest
options.rationale: Revenue ignores the cost of serving them.
Cost to serve is central to account profitability.

options.text: Raise prices for every other customer instead
options.rationale: That does not address this account's economics.

items.explanation: Correct: cost to serve can turn a big account unprofitable.
